title: Word 16 — On Conscience
attribution_note: Word 16 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Conscience as God's Law Written in the Heart

pairs.en: When God created man, He planted conscience within his soul, so that man might be guided and instructed by it, as by a rule, in what to do and what to avoid. Conscience is nothing other than the natural law, and for this reason it is akin to the written law of God. For whatever the law of God teaches, conscience teaches also.

sections.heading: Conscience Teaches Us to Know and Honor God

pairs.en: The law of God commands us to show submission, obedience, and compliance to God as the Sovereign Lord; conscience teaches the same.

sections.heading: Conscience Teaches Fear, Reverence, and Obedience

pairs.en: The law of God commands us to love God above all things; conscience commands the same, because God is the highest and supreme good and the source of every good. Therefore He must be loved above every created good.

sections.heading: Conscience Teaches Gratitude, Trust, and Honor to Parents

pairs.en: The law of God forbids harming another person or taking his life; conscience forbids the same.

sections.heading: Conscience Teaches Mercy, Purity, and Respect for What Belongs to Others

pairs.en: The law of God commands us to give to the one who asks; man hears this from his own conscience as well.

sections.heading: Conscience Forbids Deceit and Envy — and Is One with God's Law

pairs.en: Thus the law of God and conscience are alike, and lead to the same goal — our blessedness. This is why even the pagans, enlightened by philosophical learning, set down many useful precepts that came from nothing other than conscience, or the natural law, refined by much labor and study. Therefore whoever sins against conscience sins also against the law of God and against God the Lawgiver Himself. Whoever does not heed conscience does not heed the law of God, and does not heed God Himself. To disobey conscience is to disobey the law of God and God Himself. To provoke conscience is to provoke God Himself. Such Christians as sin against conscience do not truly honor God at all, but are hypocrites, for it is impossible to honor God without a clean conscience. The true Christian does not wish, and is afraid, to sin against conscience and so to break the law of God, and would rather agree to suffer than to sin. In such a conscience faith finds its rest, and it makes a person joyful. For where there is a clean conscience, there are faith and joy.

sections.heading: Conscience Convicts and Terrifies the Sinner

pairs.en: As the law of God convicts a man for his sin, so does conscience convict him. Thus it happens that when a word of reproof is spoken in general, sinners whose conscience is touched grow troubled. So fornicators grow troubled when fornication is spoken of; thieves and robbers grow troubled when theft and plunder are spoken of; flatterers and liars grow troubled when flattery and lying are spoken of, and so with the rest. That such people are troubled can be seen by certain outward signs — this is how the conviction of conscience works within them. As the law of God terrifies the sinner with the judgment of God, so does conscience terrify him, crying out within him: *man, it will go ill with you!*

Just as the workings of the law of God and of conscience are alike now, so will they be alike at the judgment of Christ. There the law of God, which the sinner has broken, will convict him, and his conscience, provoked by his sins, will convict him too. So conscience and the law of God will stand there against every sinner like two witnesses and accusers. It happens that an evil conscience seems to sleep, but when it awakens and begins to convict the sinner, then fierce torment follows from it. This is why many, unable to bear the torment of conscience, take their own lives. For as there is no rest better than that of a clean conscience, so there is no greater unrest and torment than that of an evil conscience. And if conscience tortures so severely even here, how much more will it torture the sinner in the age to come, where it will set all his sins before him and convict and torment him for them?

sections.heading: A Call to Awake and Repent

pairs.en: Sinners! Why do we sleep? Let us awake, and repent, and cleanse our sins through repentance and contrition of heart, and amend ourselves, and cease from sinning and from provoking our conscience, so that we may not appear at the judgment of Christ with an evil conscience, stained by sins, where the books of conscience will be opened and each will receive according to his deeds. Amen.
